C9000016.statement: Adversarially audit, verify, or refute OpenAI Manuscript Family 016 (Zilber–Pink in abelian varieties and the Siegel threefold.; papers: The abelian Zilber–Pink conjecture; The E×CM component of Zilber–Pink for curves in A2; Quaternionic division points on curves in the Siegel threefold; Elliptic squares and Zilber–Pink for curves in A2; Lean status: UNFORMALIZED (No Lean proof in openai/math)): either (a) discover and certify an explicit mathematical flaw, sign/orientation error, counterexample to an intermediate lemma, or statement-fidelity/citation gap with a deterministic symbolic/computational certificate (`verify.py` + `exact_certificate.json`), or (b) independently verify, repair, or generalize the manuscript's core mathematical theorem with a standalone machine-checkable certificate certified by the independent Reviewer.

C_SHARED_RESULT.statement: The common interpolation mechanism has a source-faithful, independently reviewable exact obstruction or a parameter-uniform verification theorem; this does not assert the four applications.
remaining_review: Theorem U proof and complete source coverage

C_AB_MAIN.statement: Every irreducible subvariety X of an abelian variety over a number field has finitely many maximal atypical subvarieties in its special closure (thm:main).

C_AB_NONDENSITY.statement: The abelian manuscript's thm:nondensity asserts non-density of X intersect A^[dim X+1] under its stated nondegeneracy hypotheses; those hypotheses and its proof remain unaudited.

C_AB_OPTIMAL.statement: The abelian manuscript's prop:optimal-finite deduces finiteness of optimal subvarieties from non-density and the Barroero-Dill reduction.

C_AB_MAXIMAL_OPTIMAL.statement: Every maximal atypical subvariety in the abelian manuscript's special closure is optimal (lem:maximal-optimal).

C_BD_REDUCTION.statement: The external Barroero-Dill Theorem 1.9 applies to the non-density-to-optimal-finiteness reduction as used in the abelian manuscript; source applicability is not yet checked.

C_ECM_MAIN.statement: A reduced irreducible closed Hodge-generic curve C in A_2 over Qbar contains only finitely many points whose abelian surface is isogenous to E_1 x E_2 with at least one E_i CM (thm:main).

C_ECM_ORBITS.statement: The E-times-CM manuscript claims a lower bound c times complexity(s)^(1/42) for the Galois orbit of every mixed point (thm:orbits).

C_ECM_HEIGHT_PERIOD.statement: The E-times-CM manuscript's gluing, height, essential-period and arithmetic-complexity estimates jointly give its mixed-point orbit bound; application hypotheses remain unchecked.

C_DO_CONDITIONAL.statement: Daw-Orr arXiv:1902.10483v4 Theorem 1.2 gives finiteness of the non-special E-times-CM intersection of a Hodge-generic curve under Conjecture 1.3, the large-Galois-orbit hypothesis; it does not itself give an unrestricted height estimate.

C_GR_PERIOD.statement: Gaudron-Remond Theorem 1.2 has a factor (deg_L A)^(1/g) in the numerator of its averaged inverse-square essential-period bound and a dimension-only constant; the missing-numerator attack is excluded.

C_AO.statement: The cited Andre-Oort theorem implies that a Hodge-generic algebraic curve in A_2 has finitely many special points; the primary source applicability has not been audited here.

C_QM_MAIN.statement: For a reduced irreducible closed Hodge-generic curve C in A_2 over Qbar, points with End^0(A_s) an indefinite quaternion division algebra over Q form a finite set (thm:main).

C_QM_HEIGHT.statement: At quaternionic division points, max(2,h(s)) is bounded polynomially in max(2,[K(s):K]) (thm:height).

C_QM_COMMON_RELATIONS.statement: The quaternionic application supplies common equations and global, local-positive-logarithm, coefficient and tail bounds required by thm:interpolation.

C_QM_NONIDENTITY.statement: The quaternionic application's prop:nonidentity supplies nonidentity on every relevant algebraic normalization branch, including descended varieties.

C_QM_COUNTING.statement: Quaternionic points satisfying h(t) <= A d(t)^kappa on the fixed Hodge-generic curve form a finite set (prop:counting-finiteness).

C_ES_FULL.statement: For every nonempty reduced irreducible closed Hodge-generic curve C in A_2 over Qbar, its intersection with the union of special subvarieties of dimension at most one is finite (intro:zp).

C_ES_SQUARES.statement: A nonempty reduced irreducible closed Hodge-generic curve C in A_2 over Qbar contains only finitely many elliptic-square points (intro:squares).

C_ES_HEIGHT.statement: The elliptic-square height conclusion nid:height follows if its local inputs and universal branch nonidentity meet int:height.

C_ES_LOCAL.statement: The elliptic-square application's loc:groups supplies conditions (i)-(iii) of int:height.

C_ES_NONIDENTITY.statement: The elliptic-square application's nid:nonidentity supplies condition (iv) of int:height on all relevant branches.

C_ES_COUNTING.statement: The elliptic-square manuscript's arithmetic orbit growth and definable counting argument convert its height bound into intro:squares; this argument remains unaudited.

C_ES_CLASSIFICATION.statement: The classification used in fin:classification reduces non-special points on special curves in A_2 to E-times-CM, non-CM elliptic-square, or indefinite quaternion division cases.

C_SHARED_VERIFY.statement: Under every hypothesis of elliptic int:height and quaternionic thm:interpolation, the height parameter h is polynomially bounded in d, uniformly in coefficient fields and varying descended branches.

C_SHARED_ALGEBRA.statement: Fixed-dimensional Groebner, actual-ideal membership, elimination, component and equation-recovery operations have polynomial degree bounds and bounds linear in joint logarithmic coefficient height, with no coefficient-field-degree loss.

C_SHARED_ZERO.statement: Allowed nonzero ordinary differential expressions have divisorial order divided by ord(a) bounded polynomially in the degree of the varying algebraic branch, independently of coefficient heights (int:multiplicity; lem:zero-estimate).

C_SHARED_GRAPH.statement: If f/a^m has a pole on every normalized boundary divisor of a k-dimensional affine irreducible W, its graph boundary projected to W and the constrained graph boundary a=q+g=0 have dimension at most k-2.

C_SHARED_LAYER.statement: The constrained codimension-two graph boundary yields a nonzero-on-W' polynomial P of degree <= L in the actual ideal (I,a^n,F_n), for n=rL with arbitrary prescribed polynomial r, with polynomial degree and logarithmic height controls.

C_SHARED_DESCENT.statement: Actual-ideal evaluation, small positive selected logarithms and the product formula force either a polynomial height bound or a controlled dimension drop; a fixed number of drops terminates.

C_SHARED_GENERAL.statement: Theorem U in research/shared_interpolation/interpolation.md: the complete common-relation polynomial height implication remains valid for holomorphic horizontal germs of fixed logarithmic connections at fixed centers, evaluated at finitely many fixed polynomial maps a P_i(a,U), under the stated coefficient, tail, selected-logarithm and universal normalization-branch hypotheses.

C_LOG_ZERO.statement: For a holomorphic horizontal solution of a logarithmic connection on a smooth projective curve, a nonzero f=r_0 y satisfies ord_p f <= (2 rho-1)P+Lambda+rho-1 when the first rho derivative rows have a common pole divisor of degree P and residue eigenvalues have absolute value <= Lambda; bounded-degree varying pullbacks consequently have polynomial branch-order bounds independent of coefficient heights.

C_SHARED_FORMAL_CORE.statement: For arbitrary field and matrix rank, a nonzero coefficient solution of t y'=A(t)y has its first nonzero vector coefficient in the residue eigenspace with eigenvalue its index; bounding all natural residue eigenvalues bounds that index. For all natural k,B,B',r,L with L>0 and (k+2)! B' r (2+Br+B)^k<L, one has (k+2)! B'(rL)(1+L+B(rL)+B)^k<L^(k+2).

C_LIT_BB.statement: Bertrand-Beukers 1985 Theorems 1 and 1 bis already bound polynomial-expression orders for a fixed rational differential system with holomorphic solution at zero, including singular zero; the constants depend on the system.

C_LIT_ORR.statement: Orr arXiv:2607.09565v1 Proposition 4.6 and Theorems 4.2 and 5.1 already provide selected-place, field-degree-independent G-function interpolation bounds and actual-specialization-ideal amplification under their finite arithmetic-size and nontriviality hypotheses; this comparison does not establish novelty of Theorem U.

C_SHARED_OBSTRUCTION.statement: There exists an exact source-faithful obstruction to a literal load-bearing assertion of the shared interpolation proofs; no such obstruction is asserted to have been found at scope.
